tagline: Around Wapakoneta on the homecoming parade route.
intro: This short drive through Wapakoneta, the Auglaize County seat on the Auglaize River, follows the route of the parade the town gave Neil Armstrong when he came home from the moon. It goes by the former Rhine and Brading drugstore, where he worked in high school to pay for flying lessons, and by Blume High School, where he graduated in 1947 and played baritone horn in the band.
The river's name came from French soldiers, after its clay-filled water.

moments.title: Port Koneta
moments.text: Armstrong rode his bicycle out to the Port Koneta airfield, now closed, for flying lessons, and earned his student flight certificate in August 1946, at 16, before he had a driver's license.

moments.title: Wapa Theater
moments.text: Opened in 1904 as the Brown Theater and given its neon marquee in 1939, it is where Armstrong and his classmates would have seen first-run pictures.

moments.title: Armstrong Air & Space Museum
moments.text: Built to look like a moon base, it opened on July 20, 1972, three years to the day after the first step, though Armstrong himself never had any formal connection with it.
